Technique.

Avoid training to failure for the first 2–3 weeks. Leave a recovery day between workouts.

Pain rules

01Do not aggravate symptoms

The original plan’s 0–2/10 pain range is not a guarantee of safety. Agree on acceptable loads with your clinician. Symptoms should not increase.

02Stop if symptoms worsen

Stop the exercise and consult a clinician if you get your usual right shoulder-blade pain, pain when breathing in, shooting pain, numbness or weakness. If you feel worse than usual the next day, avoid the triggering load until assessed.

When to seek urgent help

Sudden significant weakness, changes in bladder or bowel control, or numbness around the groin require urgent medical assessment. Call emergency services for chest pain or difficulty breathing.

How to progress

Add reps first, then weight. For example, for 3 × 8–12:

10 / 10 / 9 keep the same weight
12 / 12 / 12 a small increase next time

Increase weight only with consistent technique, reps in reserve and no worsening symptoms during the workout or the next day. You do not need to increase weight every week.

Balance & limitations

Use equal volume on both sides. Do not add sets to one side just because it feels weaker. A physiotherapist should guide any asymmetric correction.

For now, avoid heavy barbell squats, deadlifts, unsupported bent-over rows, good mornings, heavy shrugs and standing overhead presses.

The original control block includes dead bugs, Pallof presses, face pulls or Y-raises, and unilateral rows. These are already distributed across the week; extra volume is optional.
